newsitem.title: CANADA: Teleglobe sees 20 pct net profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Teleglobe sees 20 pct net profit growth.

text.p: Overseas telephone communications carrier Teleglobe Inc said on Thursday that it expected its net profit to increase by 20 percent in 1997, due mainly to fast growth in its international traffic.

"We're saying for the total of the year, growth of about 20 percent," Chief Financial Officer Claude Seguin told a conference call from New York, shortly after Teleglobe shares began trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

In its first quarter, Montreal-based Teleglobe's earnings jumped 54 percent to C$26.4 million or C$0.40 a share, an unusually strong first quarter fueled by a sharp upswing in global overseas traffic. The company likely would not maintain that profit growth pace through the year, Seguin said.

In the first quarter, non-Canadian global traffic accounted for 28 percent of Teleglobe's traffic, a ratio that Chief Executive Charles Sirois said he expected to grow quickly over the next two years.
"I would like that by year 2000, the global non-Canadian traffic will represent 50 percent of our traffic," Sirois said.
Teleglobe's Canadian inbound and outbound traffic was currently at about 1.6 billion minutes, while the run rate for non-Canadian international traffic was about 800 million minutes, he said.
